title: reelson video (video.json)
description: The source of truth for one video. `reelson build` regenerates video/index.html from it; every time in here is a RECORDING time (seconds in recording.mp4, as in markers.json), so trims and templates can change without re-timing anything.

title.description: Cover title: the task, e.g. "Find a customer". May hold a rotating phrase, "Automate {anything|workflows|approvals}", for a template that animates it (DEMO.title.parts); as text (captions, the upload's title) it reads with the first option.

captionTitle.description: The title as text — captions, the upload's title — when the first option of a rotating phrase does not read well (default: the title, each {a|b} as a).

subtitle.description: Cover subtitle: the benefit or context.

sections.description: Overrides reelson.config.json `sections` per slot, e.g. { "intro": "minimal", "recap": "none" }. Run `reelson templates` for the list.

intro.description: Opening section; frame 0 is the poster. Kit: poster, minimal, split.

recap.description: Steps card after the recording, or "none". Kit: steps, compact, none.

outro.description: Closing brand card. Kit: wordmark, compact, endcard.

logo.description: Overrides reelson.config.json `brand.logo`: an .svg/.png/.webp relative to the project root, or null for the text wordmark.

trim.description: The part of the recording the video uses. Prefer "auto" or a marker/click anchor: a plain number goes stale when the demo is re-recorded.

start.description: Where the footage starts: "auto" (just before the first glide or marker, i.e. after the login), { "marker": label, "offset"?: s }, { "click": n, "offset"?: s } (from the glide towards click n), or recording seconds.

end.description: Where the footage stops: { "marker": label, "offset"?: s }, { "click": n, "offset"?: s }, or recording seconds. Default: the end of the recording.

music.description: Music bed: a file (relative to the project root) for this video only, false for none, null/omitted for reelson.config.json `music.file`.

callouts.description: Numbered step pills over the recording; they also become the recap. Give each a `marker` (a markers.json label) or an `at`.

text.description: Imperative step in the UI's language, ≤ 6 words.

marker.description: markers.json label this callout is timed from.

anchor.description: Where a marker callout starts: step (default) — as the step it names begins (the first glide/click after the previous marker; a marker comes right after its action); marker — on the marker itself.

offset.description: Seconds after that start (negative: before). Keeps the callout tied to its marker when you nudge it.

at.description: Recording time instead of a marker (manual recordings).

duration.description: Seconds on screen. Default: through its step and 1.2 s past its marker (at least 3 s), ending before the next callout.

group.description: Role tag (two-actor videos). Default: taken from the hand-off cards.

say.description: Voice-over ("voice": true): what is spoken for this step, when it should differ from the text (e.g. a full sentence); false: nothing.

position.description: Where it sits over the footage (landscape, square). Default: `calloutPosition`.

calloutPosition.description: Where the callouts sit over the footage (landscape, square): auto (default) — at the bottom, moving to the top while they would cover what the cursor works on; top / bottom — always there. A callout's `position` overrides it.

voice.description: Voice-over: true speaks each callout (its `say`, else its text) with the reelson.config.json `voice` provider (OpenAI by default; ElevenLabs, a local Piper voice or a local command); lines are cached in <demo>/voice/. An object turns it on with this video's own provider / model / voice / instructions / speed and may add an `intro` line spoken over the intro.

provider.description: This video's provider, from its defaults (baseURL, command and options stay with the project's provider).

intro.description: Spoken over the intro, e.g. the title as a sentence.

publish.description: How `reelson publish` words this video. Without it: the title, and a description made of the subtitle and the numbered steps (callouts); each channel's footer and tags are added.

title.description: The upload's title (default: captionTitle, else the title as text).

description.description: The upload's description (default: subtitle + the steps).

formats.description: Versions every `reelson render` adds besides the 16:9 one, as with --portrait / --square. A square version needs the square take (`reelson record --square`); without one it is skipped with a note.

portrait.description: Source of `reelson render --portrait`: mobile = the phone take (`reelson record --mobile`), desktop = a camera framing each element on the desktop recording, auto (default) = the phone take when there is one.

cursor.description: The cursor layer (recordings with record.cursor "layer", the default since reelson 0.4): false hides it, or tune it. Has no effect when the cursor is filmed in.

size.description: Arrow size in recording CSS px. Default 44 (the classic macOS-style arrow).

ripple.description: The brand-coloured ring on each press. Default true.

idle.description: Fade the cursor out after this many seconds without moving or clicking, back in as it moves again. Default 0 (always shown).

lag.description: Seconds to draw the cursor later than logged, for a page that paints late (a heavy page, a drag): the page's response then lands under the cursor, not behind it. Default 0.

zooms.description: Zoom-ins on the framed recording. Prefer `clicks`: timing and focus are computed from the cursor so the zoom rides along with the glide.

clicks.description: [first, last] click numbers (1-based, markers.json `clicks`) the zoom frames. Timing and focus are computed.

follow.description: Pan with the cursor while zoomed, so the clicks need not fit one view (recordings with a logged cursor, record.cursor "layer"). Default false.

x.description: Focus point, fraction of the frame width. Default: centred on the clicks.

y.description: Focus point, fraction of the frame height.

at.description: Manual zoom: recording time the zoom-in starts (instead of `clicks`).

duration.description: Manual zoom: seconds from zoom-in start to zoomed-out.

click.description: 1-based click in markers.json `clicks`: the time the cursor starts gliding towards it.
